question: Why do midwives take routine measurements like blood pressure and weight?

options.A: To fulfill hospital administrative record-keeping duties
options.B: To guide critical clinical decisions for patient care
options.C: To practice using complex medical equipment daily
options.D: To compare different patients against each other

explanation: Measurements provide clear numbers that help midwives make important assessments and care choices. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is using proper technique important when taking a patient's measurements?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing hospital supplies
options.B: It ensures the recorded numbers reflect the patient's actual state
options.C: It speeds up the process of discharging patients from the ward
options.D: It prevents the medical equipment from ever needing calibration

explanation: Good technique minimizes errors so the data accurately represents the patient's true condition. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h1)

question: In healthcare measurements, what does accuracy mean?

options.A: How clean the surface of the measuring tool is
options.B: How many times a measurement can be repeated
options.C: How close a measured value is to the true value
options.D: How fast a clinical instrument can be turned on

explanation: Accuracy tells us how close a recorded result is to the actual, correct standard. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h2)

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if the sphygmomanometer needle starts above zero?

options.A: The accuracy of the measurement is compromised
options.B: The patient's actual blood pressure will instantly rise
options.C: The precision of the device automatically increases
options.D: The measurement becomes completely impossible to take

explanation: A baseline error shifts every reading away from the true value, making it less accurate. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h2)

question: How is precision best described in clinical measurement?

options.A: The speed at which a nurse records data on a chart
options.B: The exact distance between the tool and the patient
options.C: The closeness of repeated measurements to one another
options.D: The official factory price of a medical instrument

explanation: Precision refers to how consistent and reproducible results are when repeated. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Can a set of clinical measurements be precise without being accurate?

options.A: Yes, but only if digital equipment is used instead of analog tools
options.B: Yes, if repeated values are close together but far from the true value
options.C: No, an inaccurate tool cannot produce consistent readings ever
options.D: No, precision automatically guarantees that the true value is found

explanation: Consistent results grouped together show high precision, but a calibration error can make them all incorrect. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h3)

question: A thermometer reads 39.5°C, 39.6°C, and 39.5°C for a healthy patient whose true temperature is 36.8°C. What does this show?
explanation: The readings are close to each other, showing precision, but far from the real temperature, showing low accuracy. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why do midwives aim for both high accuracy and high precision in clinical practice?

options.A: To avoid having to check vital signs more than once a day
options.B: To satisfy hospital regulations without actually helping patients
options.C: To ensure patient assessments are both consistent and truly correct
options.D: To make sure digital machines never require battery replacements

explanation: Combining both qualities guarantees that measurements are dependable, reproducible, and reflect reality. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which type of measurement error is predictable and shifts all readings consistently in one direction?
explanation: Systematic errors consistently push results away from the true value in the same direction, often due to calibration issues. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is a common feature of random errors in clinical settings?

options.A: They are caused only by factory defects in weighing scales
options.B: They always make every recorded measurement much higher
options.C: They fluctuate unpredictably above and below the true value
options.D: They can be completely eliminated by using new digital tools

explanation: Random errors happen by chance during the measurement process, causing scatter around the true value. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is an effective way to minimize systematic errors in clinical equipment?

options.A: Asking the patient to guess their own vital signs
options.B: Using older analog devices instead of digital ones
options.C: Recording measurements only at the end of a shift

explanation: Regular calibration ensures that instruments read true values and removes persistent bias. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h6)

question: A midwife is about to check a patient's blood pressure in the antenatal clinic. What action helps prevent measurement errors?

options.A: Talking to the patient about unrelated topics while pumping
options.B: Wrapping the blood pressure cuff loosely over heavy clothing
options.C: Keeping the patient standing up quickly to save time
options.D: Supporting the patient's arm at the level of the heart

explanation: Proper arm positioning prevents gravity and height differences from distorting the blood pressure reading. [learn more](BMP112_U1_T2#BMP112_U1_T2_h6)
